jobs.title: Data Analyst, Population Health Management
jobs.description:
Overview

Reporting to the SVP for Population and Community Health, this position works collaboratively across teams to develop and maintain data collection, measurement tools and databases to support data analysis in support of population health, community health and managed care initiatives.

As part of the ongoing work of One Brooklyn Health to transform healthcare delivery in Central Brooklyn, the Population and Community Health team works to eliminate racial and gender health inequities rooted in historical and contemporary injustices, by improving health outcomes, addressing social drivers and using data for advocacy.

Responsibilities

Designing and building population health data set processes for purposes such as modeling, production or mining.
Performing and interpreting population health data studies to learn more about new data sources or new uses for existing ones.
Develop reports, dashboards, scorecards, and other analytics results as necessary to support activities related to population health and other strategic goals.
Analyze, interpret and generate reports on performance related to overall outcomes, utilization, risk adjusted total costs of care, population health and care coordination.
Support the analysis of data from multiple sources, primarily claims files associated with value-based contracts.
Provide insight for informed decision-making and planning by identifying trends/patterns within complex data sets and visualizing and deploying the data to appropriately inform stakeholders.
Develop innovative recommendations to achieve successes related to population health management initiatives and impact quality and efficiency in the delivery model, resulting in a positive impact to clinical and financial outcomes.
Serve as subject matter expert to support the population health needs regarding claims data, value-based contracts, and quality data.
Develop and maintain quality control standards and data reconciliation techniques for internal and external reporting.
Create and maintain documentation relating to data management including training guides, report specifications, and data dictionaries.
Adhere to reporting deadlines for assigned reports.

Qualifications

Position Requirements:

Bachelor's Degree BA/BS in computer science, statistics, and/or public health or related field (required).
Master's Degree Master’s in Business, Health Administration, Finance or other preferred.
5 years Minimum of five (5) to ten (10) years of experience working with data visualization software such as Tableau, Power BI, Qlik, etc. preferred.
3 years Minimum of three (3) to five (5) years of experience working with statistical programming languages such as R or Python (Preferred) Knowledge of CMS, TJC and other applicable regulations.
Fluent in MS Office, including MS Excel and MS PowerPoint.
Experience with EPIC Reporting.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Strong conceptual analytical and quantitative skills.
Strong data collection, manipulation, and analysis skills.
An informed perspective on embedding and applying a racial and gender justice lens in decision-making, planning and implementation.
Familiarity with SQL programming language concepts
Experience with health insurance claims structure and analytics, including GPRO/HEDIS Quality measures, risk adjustment methodologies, efficiency of care and utilization metrics.
Experience with large data sets, clinical quality measures, and claims analysis. Experience with data sets typically found in a health plan environment, including claims data, care management and care planning data, provider network management data, etc.
Intermediate to Advanced level knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite including Excel, Word and PowerPoint. Advanced skills in Excel and ease with data management concepts (i.e. MS Access, SQL). Skill in oral and written communication and time management with ability to effectively present to and facilitate groups
Experience presenting technical data and information to non-technical users.
Working knowledge of finance, accounting, financial models, healthcare data, market and competitive analysis techniques
Interest in and active pursuit of opportunities to learn and grow, and ability to handle multiple demands, shifting priorities, crises, and rapid change.

Project Solutions Engineer

This is a fulltime first shift position (Monday – Friday) 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM

Position Overview

The Project Solutions Engineer serves as an in-house engineering resource for the Business Development and Project Sales teams, with a focus on reviewing opportunities early, strengthening technical recommendations, and helping move qualified projects from initial review to a clearly scoped, specifiable solution. This role is intended to provide practical engineering judgment, support customer-facing technical credibility, and help give the buyer or specifying engineer confidence in EFG’s design recommendations.

The position supports the BD team by reviewing project information as opportunities come in, commenting on design considerations, identifying risks or gaps, and helping determine whether EFG’s recommended solution is technically appropriate. The role should keep the BD team involved in the customer relationship while reducing the time spent on detailed technical review, design interpretation, and engineering coordination.

For candidates with Professional Engineer licensure, this role may include responsible review and stamping of applicable project work once the individual has developed sufficient familiarity with EFG’s process, standards, products, and internal controls. Use of a professional stamp must be based on sound engineering judgment, proper review, and comfort with the scope of responsibility.

Review specifications, drawings, and project data early in the opportunity process to evaluate feasibility, application fit, and technical risk.
Provide practical design comments and engineering recommendations that support BD discussions with buyers, engineers, and project stakeholders.
Help translate customer needs, site conditions, and project requirements into technically sound, cost-conscious system solutions.
Assess hydraulic, civil, electrical, structural, and site-specific considerations to identify concerns before proposals or recommendations are finalized.
Prepare early-stage documentation, including technical summaries, design assumptions, equipment recommendations, review notes, and preliminary layouts.
Prepare design reports, engineering review packages, and supporting documentation for review by external engineers or other qualified reviewers.
Participate in client calls, site visits, pre-bid discussions, and engineer-facing conversations when technical credibility or clarification is needed.
Collaborate with Business Development, Project Sales, internal engineering resources, and external subject matter experts to refine defensible system designs, proposal strategy, and project handoff.
Support responsible engineering review of applicable project work, including stamped work where appropriate based on licensure, review standards, and scope of responsibility.
Maintain current knowledge of EFG products, component manufacturers, industry standards, and application best practices.

Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering or related engineering discipline required.
Active Professional Engineer license required or strongly preferred; Civil PE or PE with directly relevant water/wastewater, municipal infrastructure, pump station, or site development experience preferred.
5+ years of relevant experience in civil, water/wastewater, pump station, utility, or infrastructure-related engineering preferred.
Demonstrated ability to review plans, specifications, submittals, and project requirements and provide practical engineering recommendations.
Comfortable working directly with Business Development and Sales teams in a fast-moving opportunity environment.
Ability and willingness, where properly licensed and supported by adequate review, to take professional responsibility for applicable engineering work.
Solid understanding of pumps, hydraulics, site layout considerations, and project design coordination.
Excellent technical writing, communication, and judgment skills.

Position Title

Program Coordinator - Regional Hub (THRIVE)

Job Family Group

Professional Staff

Job Description Summary

The Regional Hub Program Coordinator provides operational and administrative support for the Thrive Kansas Digital Mental Health Initiative within an assigned Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) regional hub. This position coordinates day-to-day implementation activities, training and onboarding logistics, meeting and communication activities, documentation and record management, and project tracking. The role serves as a key resource for participating sites, community health workers (CHWs), providers, implementation partners, and regional leadership, helping ensure regional activities are completed efficiently, consistently, and in alignment with project timelines, reporting requirements, and continuous quality improvement (CQI) processes.

The Thrive Kansas Digital Mental Health Initiative is a grant funded, statewide, evidence-based digital therapeutic strategy designed to expand access to treatment for depression, substance use disorders (SUD) and other mental disorders in rural Kansas. The initiative deploys clinically validated computerized mental health interventions supported by community-based facilitation and integrated into rural primary care, behavioral health, and community settings.

We are currently recruiting for three program coordinator positions.

Job Description

Job Duties

Regional Deployment & Site Coordination

Track completion of regional onboarding, deployment, and access setup activities for participating sites. Maintain deployment task lists, implementation documentation, and project records.
Schedule and coordinate deployment-related meetings and communications. Log, monitor, and route technical issues to appropriate project personnel and track issue resolution.
Maintain records related to deployment activities, onboarding progress, implementation milestones, and site readiness.
Support the Regional Hub Program Manager in monitoring implementation progress, identifying potential barriers, and facilitating successful deployment activities.

Training Coordination & Implementation Support

Schedule and coordinate regional training sessions for providers, CHWs, supervisors, navigators, and program staff. Track training attendance, completion, certifications, and related documentation. Distribute training materials, reminders, schedules, and follow-up communications. Serve as the first point of contact for routine implementation questions and assist with resolving common operational concerns.
Support onboarding and implementation activities for participating sites, organizations, and staff. Coordinate logistics and facilitate stakeholder communication to support successful adoption of digital mental health services.

Workforce & Program Operations Support

Support onboarding logistics for CHWs, case management staff, and other program personnel. Maintain regional staffing rosters, contact lists, distribution lists, and workforce documentation.
Coordinate routine communication among CHWs, supervisors, project staff, and participating organizations, and track operational issues and implementation barriers affecting program activities.
Document workflow modifications, process updates, and operational improvements to help ensure consistency across participating sites and regional partners.

Evaluation, Reporting & Continuous Quality Improvement

Track regional data submission schedules, reporting deadlines, and project deliverables. Coordinate meetings associated with evaluation activities, reporting reviews, and CQI initiatives.
Document meeting notes, action items, decisions, and follow-up tasks, and maintain records for grant administration, reporting, and project documentation.
Support preparation and dissemination of summaries, reports, presentations, slide decks, and stakeholder communications.
Assist the Regional Hub Program Manager in monitoring completion of CQI action items and reporting requirements.

User Support & Access Coordination

Coordinate logistics associated with participant, provider, and stakeholder support activities. Track access-related issues reported by users, CHWs, providers, and participating sites.
Route user access concerns to the appropriate technical or program staff and monitor progress toward resolution. Maintain user-facing support materials, frequently asked questions (FAQs), reference guides, and communication resources.
Track recurring access barriers and support identification of trends that require escalation to regional leadership or project management teams.

Regional Communication & Stakeholder Support

Support communication among participating healthcare organizations, community partners, providers, and project teams within the regional hub.
Coordinate meeting logistics, maintain distribution lists, prepare communications, and facilitate follow-up activities related to project implementation.
Assist in maintaining positive relationships with participating organizations and stakeholders.
Support dissemination of project updates, training opportunities, implementation resources, and program information throughout the region.

Integration with Regional & Statewide Program Operations

Support the Regional Hub Program Manager in ensuring alignment between regional implementation activities and statewide project goals.
Maintain documentation, records, and communications that support coordination across regional hubs and statewide leadership teams.
Participate in statewide coordination meetings, implementation activities, and quality improvement initiatives as assigned.
Assist in sharing lessons learned, implementation best practices, and operational insights across project teams and partner organizations.
Conducts activities in a professional and ethical manner, and in accordance with KUMC Policies and applicable local, state and federal laws and regulations.
Performs job responsibilities in a safe and secure manner.
Coordinate work with other University areas ensure integration and support of the University mission.
Develops, maintains and expands job-specific knowledge and skills to keep pace with industry changes and supports the university's commitment to excellence and innovation.
Participates in relevant committees, task force, or other similar activities.
Maintain confidentiality of medical center, employee, and patient information. Manages sensitive data with discretion and in accordance with KUMC policies and legal requirements.
Maintains the highest standards of integrity, respect, professional conduct, and ethical standards.

new_jobs.description:
Job Summary

TCU Global supports all undergraduate student programs abroad and away, as well as graduate students, faculty, and staff engaged in international experiences. TCU Global Program Coordinators serve as the first contact for students going abroad. They are responsible for providing student-centric, professional, and engaged advising to support student success. Program coordinators are committed to assisting students in identifying opportunities for study abroad while fulfilling their graduation requirements and achieving career, personal, and educational goals. Program coordinators work directly with students, faculty, departments, and schools to ensure that the undergraduate courses offered abroad are approved for TCU credit.

The Program Coordinator provides the necessary administrative support to all TCU Global programs. The position coordinates pre-departure preparations including orientations; advises students; manages departmental marketing; promotes the various programs while working in collaboration with partners abroad; supports students, parents and other stakeholders when critical situations develop; conducts overseas site visits as necessary for program orientations, in conjunction with TCU Global staff supervision.

Duties & Essential Job Functions

Acts as an advisor for TCU Global programs, including semester, summer, and faculty-led. This includes creating advising calendars, curating online advising content, updating the TCU Calendar, and advising students on the various programs offered.
Coordinates and manages events and presentations, including: information sessions, tabling events, TCU Admission events, classroom presentation requests, TCU Orientation, pre-departure mixers, and reentry receptions, among others. Assist with the Study Abroad Fair and any other TCU Global initiatives.
Manages TCU Global marketing, which includes: creating a social media calendar, organizing a TCU Global brand kit, creating content for webpage/printed brochures/Instagram/advertisements/tabling events/etc., managing the Social Media Ambassadors, among other things.
Serves as the staff advisor for the TCU Global Ambassadors student organization.
Assists with the development and coordination of TCU’s global learning initiatives through pre-departure orientations.
Performs partner institution visitations for on-site orientations for programs. These visits may include program evaluation.
Assists appropriate TCU Global staff with reviewing current application materials for relevance, program requirements, and accessible design.
Using attendance statistics and feedback surveys, evaluates popularity of programs and makes recommendations to the Director regarding improvements, new opportunities, or ways to address student concerns.
Works with TCU Global team to evaluate accessibility of programs and representation of student diversity abroad and to supports study abroad accessibility efforts through financial advising, cross-departmental collaboration, and peer-to-peer outreach
Performs other related duties as assigned.

Required Education & Experience

Bachelor’s degree and 3 years relevant work experience in international programs or in a higher education environment with responsibilities in program development or program administration

OR

Master’s degree and 1 year relevant work experience in international programs or in a higher education environment with responsibilities in program development or program administration
